import pandas as pd

def main():
    # File paths for source data
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_8/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_8/test_1.csv"
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_8/target_multisource_cot.csv"

    # Load source tables
    # Source 0 schema: ['track_id', 'dummy']
    df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)
    # Source 1 schema: ['index_track', 'track_id']
    df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path)

    # Inspect schemas:
    # df0: track_id, dummy
    # df1: index_track, track_id

    # Goal: Target schema ['index_track', 'track_id', 'dummy']

    # Plan:
    # - Source0 has track_id and dummy, but no index_track
    # - Source1 has index_track and track_id, but no dummy
    # - We want to combine these two sources to get all three columns.
    #
    # Since both have track_id, we can join on track_id to combine index_track and dummy.
    #
    # Join df1 (index_track, track_id) with df0 (track_id, dummy) on 'track_id'.
    #
    # This will produce a dataframe with columns: index_track, track_id, dummy
    #
    # After join, keep only these columns and write to target CSV.

    # Perform inner join on 'track_id'
    df_merged = pd.merge(df1, df0, on='track_id', how='inner')

    # Reorder columns to match target schema
    df_target = df_merged[['index_track', 'track_id', 'dummy']]

    # Save to CSV without index column
    df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
